## Findings
- claim-1: For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and each proposed Schur family has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-6@L18-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: For rectangular data \((r,q,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\), the LR presentation has \(27\) basis elements and \(327\) relation vectors; its computed SNF has \(25\) unit factors and no nonunit factors, so \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^2\). [artifact bfbfd736e27f1a193b24aab07cfae4f512c6c9dd5039963e396331b46516f16f]
- claim-3: For rectangular data \((r,q,i,j)=(5,2,1,1)\), the LR presentation has \(20\) basis elements and \(179\) relation vectors; its computed SNF has \(18\) unit factors and no nonunit factors, so \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^2\). [artifact bfbfd736e27f1a193b24aab07cfae4f512c6c9dd5039963e396331b46516f16f]
- claim-4: In both cases \(a=b=1\), hence \(N=2\), and the two candidate families specialize to \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(2)}\}\) and \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(1,1)}\}\). Conditional on the established generation theorem and the two computed cokernels, each family is irredundant: deletion would make \(\mathbb Z^2\) cyclic, which is impossible.
- claim-5: These computations concern rectangular Schur-data only; no permutation \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) admissibility is asserted.
## Strategy
Rebuild both finite LR presentation matrices using right-to-left row reading and standard lattice-prefix checks. Include the two stated regression coefficients before forming relations. Independently reproduce each matrix and Smith normal form by a separate implementation or a Pieri/LR cross-check. Treat results solely for \((r,q,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\) and \((5,2,1,1)\) rectangular Schur data.

## Gaps
The existing SNF artifacts are invalidated by the LR reading-order defect. No corrected computation, independent reproduction, or permutation-admissibility correspondence is presently established.

## Next
Compute corrected SNFs for both cases; record matrix dimensions, regression outcomes, invariant factors, and reproducibility comparison. Only if both computations agree may the resulting quotient structure be used with graded Nakayama to assess irredundance of the two \(N=2\) Schur families.
